items.headline: TRAI proposes 5G network-slice notice, capacity and QoS requirements from 1 October 2026, plus outage reporting and subscriber rebates.

summary.text: This is a consultation, not an operative amendment. Stakeholder comments were invited by 26 August 2026, with counter-comments due by 7 September 2026.

cite.quote: by 26th August 2026  and counter comments by 7th September 2026.

summary.text: If adopted, service providers planning a new 5G network slice would have to notify TRAI at least 21 days in advance and demonstrate sufficient capacity across the relevant cells.

cite.quote: Every service provider, planning to create a new network slice in their 5G network, shall submit the details of proposed and existing network slice parameters, at least twenty one (21) days in advance to the Authority

summary.text: The draft would also introduce network-performance benchmarks from 1 October 2026, including reporting significant outages within 24 hours and rebates or validity extensions for outages exceeding 24 hours.

cite.quote: Rebate to the subscribers for significant network outages of more than 24 hrs:

relevance.why: The proposal regulates telecom service providers’ quality of service and 5G network slicing, rather than artificial-intelligence activities or AI providers directly.

items.title: Consultation on Draft Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026.
items.headline: TRAI proposes advance A2P call declarations and AI/ML-driven UCC escalation when five CLIs are flagged within ten days.

summary.text: TRAI has proposed amendments applying across India; they would take effect 30 days after publication in the Official Gazette. The changes are not yet in force.

cite.quote: These regulations shall apply throughout the territory of India. (3) These shall come into force after thirty days from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.

summary.text: Every sender would have to declare use of application-to-person voice calls to the originating access provider in advance. An undeclared A2P call would be treated as unsolicited commercial communication.

cite.quote: Every Sender shall declare to the Originating Access Provider, in advance, about the use of Application-to-Person (A2P) calls.

summary.text: The proposal would require access providers to use AI/ML-based UCC_Detect systems to flag suspected spam CLIs and share them through the DLT platform. Where five or more CLIs linked to a sender are flagged within ten days, escalating KYC and service restrictions would apply.

cite.quote: if it is found that five  or more CLIs of the sender have been flagged as “Suspected UCC CLI” within the last ten  days, all the concerned OAPs shall take action against the sender as follows:

summary.text: TRAI is seeking stakeholder comments on the draft by 12 April 2026, with counter-comments due by 27 April 2026. These are consultation deadlines, not compliance deadlines under a final regulation.

cite.quote: The stakeholders may give their counter comments by 27 th April, 2026, which may be sent preferably in electronic form to Sh Deepak Sharma, Advisor (QoS-Il), TRAI, on mail-id advqos@trai.gov.in

relevance.why: The proposal concerns telecom providers and senders of commercial voice calls, using AI/ML spam detection; it is not a general AI governance measure.
relevance.action: Assess whether any existing or planned voice outreach involves A2P calls; if so, consider submitting comments by 12 April 2026.

items.title: Consultation Paper on Review of Rating of Properties for Digital Connectivity Regulations, 2024
items.headline: TRAI proposes amendments to property digital-connectivity ratings and invites stakeholder comments by 23 March 2026.

summary.text: TRAI is consulting on amendments to the 2024 framework for rating properties according to digital-connectivity readiness, including proposed changes to the Regulations and Rating Manual.

cite.quote: Stakeholders are requested to submit their comments, feedback, and suggestions on the proposed amendments and on any other aspects of Rating of Properties for Digital Connectivity Regulations, 2024, preferably

summary.text: The consultation covers proposed amendments to both the regulatory text and the Rating Manual. Stakeholder submissions are requested by 23 March 2026.

cite.quote: Accordingly, the scope of this consultation paper is to seek views of stakeholders on the proposed amendments in Regulation placed at Chapter 4 and proposed amendments in Rating Manual in Chapter 5.

relevance.why: The paper concerns telecom and property digital-connectivity ratings, not artificial-intelligence regulation or AI activities.

items.headline: India publishes amendments to digital-connectivity property-rating rules; the supplied text reveals no AI-related requirement.

summary.text: The supplied Gazette extract is materially garbled. It appears to contain numbered amendments to the 2024 regulations, but the operative substitutions and additions cannot be read reliably.

The readable material concerns digital-connectivity property-rating bands, including thresholds from 25 to 88, rather than artificial-intelligence regulation. No AI-specific obligation is identifiable in the supplied text.

relevance.why: The instrument concerns property ratings for digital connectivity, not AI regulation, and the supplied text contains no identifiable AI requirement.

items.title: Notification - Updated contact details of Auditors to Audit the accuracy of Metering and Billing Systems of the service providers.
items.headline: TRAI has updated the contact details of nine empanelled agencies auditing providers’ metering and billing systems.

summary.text: The notification confirms nine audit agencies remain empanelled for three years from 22 February 2024 to audit service providers’ metering and billing accuracy under the 2023 regulation.

cite.quote: the Authority conveyed the empaneled of nine Audit Agencies as auditor to audit the accuracy of metering & Billing system of service providers for a period of three years

summary.text: It supplies updated contact details for those agencies in Annexure I. The notification does not introduce a new AI requirement or change the audit framework.

cite.quote: In continuation to the above referred letter, kindly ﬁnd the updated contact details of empaneled audit agencies attached at Annexure-I.

relevance.why: The notice concerns telecom metering and billing audit contacts, not artificial-intelligence regulation or AI activities.
